summary: 10 concrete, comment-endorsed recommendations from a verified full crawl of the HN front page.
telegram_footer: 10 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: Artificial Intelligence Natural Stupidity
items.summary: A security talk on why human oversight cannot reliably catch LLM mistakes.
items.why_included: A commenter specifically called it a great security talk with a sharp automation-safety framing.
items.evidence: A commenter praised its comparison between pilots catching automation errors and people catching LLM mistakes.

evidence_sources.author: washbasin
evidence_sources.excerpt: Great security talk about how humans aren't setup to deal with LLMs as tools. I love the bullet point(s) : we don't trust [aircraft] pilots to catch automations mistakes (e.g. autopilot), but we are expecting humans to catch LLM mistakes.

items.name: Bonsai
items.summary: Jane Street's OCaml library for dense, interactive web and terminal interfaces.
items.why_included: HN commenters valued its utility-first interface model and reported using its terminal implementation.
items.evidence: One commenter called the library great for fast, pleasant, information-dense tools; another uses its terminal implementation for contacts.

evidence_sources.author: MrBuddyCasino
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is great. It focuses on utility and information density over design. It looks like someone took a terminal UI and transplanted it to the web, Bloomberg terminal style. I'm pretty sure you can build tools with this that are fast and pleasant to use.

evidence_sources.author: avsm
evidence_sources.excerpt: There's a full terminal implementation of Bonsai as well. I actually use it in my personal workflow these days to manage my contacts database!

items.name: Isopolis
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Isopolis – Isometric pixel map of SF
items.summary: An explorable isometric pixel-art map of San Francisco neighborhoods and landmarks.
items.why_included: A commenter independently praised its interactive neighborhood exploration and SimCity-like feel.
items.evidence: A commenter called it really cool and highlighted the clickable neighborhoods and regions.

evidence_sources.author: accrual
evidence_sources.excerpt: This is really cool, it gives me SimCity 2000 vibes. I like that I can click on neighborhoods and regions and get more information about them!

items.name: Floor796
items.source_story_title: Show HN: Isopolis – Isometric pixel map of SF
items.summary: A huge interactive pixel-art world filled with discoverable scenes and characters.
items.why_included: It surfaced as a strongly praised reference for deep, scrollable pixel-art exploration.
items.evidence: A commenter described Floor796 as easy to keep browsing and exploring, then linked it directly.

evidence_sources.author: murphyslab
evidence_sources.excerpt: Incredible. It's easy to just go on browsing and exploring. The massive, scrollable pixel art aspect reminds me a little of Floor796:

items.name: SmallDocs
items.source_story_title: Prevent cognitive debt by manually retyping LLM-generated code
items.summary: An open-source tool for agent-generated, human-readable Markdown code walkthroughs.
items.why_included: A practitioner uses it to stay connected to code produced by coding agents.
items.evidence: Its author says they use SmallDocs frequently to stay in touch with LLM-generated code.

evidence_sources.author: FailMore
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use this a lot to stay in touch with the code the LLM is producing.

items.name: Rspamd
items.source_story_title: What DMARC Protects You From, and What It Does Not
items.summary: An open-source mail filter that includes inbound DMARC validation.
items.why_included: It was directly recommended by users as a maintained alternative for receiving-side DMARC checks.
items.evidence: Two commenters reported using Rspamd, with one citing its DMARC module and broader inbound-mail use.

evidence_sources.author: oogali
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use rspamd. This might be a little heavy if you’re solely looking for DMARC validation, but I use the other parts of rspamd as well for inbound email.

evidence_sources.author: 1over137
evidence_sources.excerpt: Indeed opendmarc seems practically abandonware. rspamd is what I use.

items.name: C-Kermit
items.source_story_title: Celebrating 45 Years of Kermit with the First New C-Kermit Release in 15 Years
items.summary: A mature communications toolkit with inline file transfer over SSH sessions.
items.why_included: A commenter highlighted its useful SSH file-transfer workflow and open-source availability.
items.evidence: A commenter called its inline transfer over an open SSH session a useful quick transfer path.

evidence_sources.author: donflamenco
evidence_sources.excerpt: One cool feature is that you can use C-Kermit to do inline file transfers over the open SSH session. It doesn't work over a terminal muxer like screen/tmux, but it is pretty useful for a quick way to transfer files between the client and the remote host.

items.name: Signals and Threads: Building a UI Framework
items.summary: A Jane Street podcast episode about the design and implementation of Bonsai.
items.why_included: A commenter singled it out as a great episode for understanding the UI library.
items.evidence: A commenter explicitly recommended the episode as a great Signals and Threads discussion of this work.

evidence_sources.author: bsmith89
evidence_sources.excerpt: There's a great Signals and Threads (Jane Street's Podcast) episode about this work:

items.name: Colatura di Alici
items.source_story_title: Decades-old fish sauce at abandoned factory in Canada finally being removed
items.summary: An Italian anchovy fish sauce used to add concentrated umami to dishes.
items.why_included: A first-hand user called it magical, versatile, and especially useful in pasta dishes.
items.evidence: A commenter described Colatura di Alici as a genuinely magical ingredient and said they use it often in pasta.

evidence_sources.author: BoxOfRain
evidence_sources.excerpt: Despite the fearsome smell when it’s collected together in bulk, modern garum in the form of Colatura di Alici is a genuinely magical ingredient. It’s very similar to what the Romans used, except it’s made exclusively from anchovies whereas the Romans used many varieties of fish to make garum. I use it often in pasta dishes especially, but it’s a versatile ingredient for adding umami in general.

items.name: A Handwritten Blogging Platform
items.source_story_title: Show HN: A Handwritten Blogging Platform
items.summary: A publishing platform for blogs and comments written and shared by hand.
items.why_included: The physical-medium interaction drew direct praise from a reader who enjoyed handwritten comments.
items.evidence: A commenter said they loved that some platform comments are handwritten too.

evidence_sources.author: jonas21
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love that the comments on some of the posts (like this one) are written by hand too!
